**Esprima** ([example.invalid](http://example.invalid), BSD license) is a high performance,
standard-compliant [ECMAScript](http://example.invalid/publications/standards/Ecma-262.htm)
parser written in ECMAScript (also popularly known as
[JavaScript](https://example.invalid/wiki/JavaScript)).
Esprima is created and maintained by [Ariya Hidayat](https://example.invalid/ariyahidayat),
with the help of [many contributors](https://example.invalid/jquery/esprima/contributors).

### Features

- Full support for ECMAScript 6 ([ECMA-262](http://example.invalid/publications/standards/Ecma-262.htm))
- Sensible [syntax tree format](https://example.invalid/estree/estree/blob/master/spec.md) as standardized by [ESTree project](https://example.invalid/estree/estree)
- Optional tracking of syntax node location (index-based and line-column)
- [Heavily tested](http://example.invalid/test/ci.html) (~1250 [unit tests](https://example.invalid/jquery/esprima/tree/master/test/fixtures) with [full code coverage](https://example.invalid/github/jquery/esprima))

Esprima serves as a **building block** for some JavaScript
language tools, from [code instrumentation](http://example.invalid/demo/functiontrace.html)
to [editor autocompletion](http://example.invalid/demo/autocomplete.html).

Esprima runs on many popular web browsers, as well as other ECMAScript platforms such as
[Rhino](http://example.invalid/rhino), [Nashorn](http://example.invalid/projects/nashorn/), and [Node.js](https://example.invalid/package/esprima).

For more information, check the web site [example.invalid](http://example.invalid).
